label: Vista Composition
description: Landscape composition craft — how the frame organizes land, sky and distance, from grand vistas to quiet corners.

items.name: low-horizon-sky
items.text: horizon dropped into the lowest third, the sky given four-fifths of the frame to perform

items.name: high-horizon-foreground
items.text: horizon pinned high, the foreground ground plane unrolling toward the viewer in deep textured perspective

items.name: s-curve-lead
items.text: a river or shoreline drawn as a silver S-curve, pulling the eye from the near corner to the far light

items.name: foreground-anchor
items.text: a bold foreground anchor at arm's length — cracked rock, ice, flowers — with the vista receding behind it in three distinct planes

items.name: layered-recession
items.text: ridge upon ridge receding in tonal steps, each layer paler and softer than the last, depth built entirely from atmosphere

items.name: lone-element
items.text: one small element allowed to matter — a single tree, boulder or reed — held in generous negative space

items.name: mirror-symmetry
items.text: a still-water reflection folding the scene into perfect bilateral symmetry, the waterline as the fold

items.name: pattern-field
items.text: the land itself as pattern — dunes, furrows, ice plates — repeating to the frame edge with a single interruption for scale

items.name: frame-within
items.text: the vista framed through a natural arch, cave mouth or branch window, darkness ringing the bright distance

items.name: diagonal-drive
items.text: one strong diagonal running corner to corner — a ridge line, a shadow edge — keeping the stillness charged

items.name: telephoto-slice
items.text: a long-lens slice cut from the greater landscape, layers compressed flat, geography abstracted into shape and tone

items.name: scale-tree
items.text: a lone tree set small against a colossal landform, the size gap between them becoming the story of the frame
